author: Greg Mocker
title: Animal shelter in Long Island City networks to save pets - NewsBreak
text:
By Greg Mocker ,
2 hours ago
QUEENS, N.Y. (PIX11) — Animal shelters in the city have been over capacity this summer, and the next season usually brings in more pets.
A shelter in Queens is networking with other locations around the region and country to save as many dogs and cats as they can.
More Local News NYC Second Chance Rescue creates new lives for abandoned and abused animals.
The Second Chance Rescue facility fills two floors of the entire building on 37th Avenue.
Currently, 35 cats call it home, and there’s room for 12 large dogs.
Co-founder Jennifer Brooks said this location opened in 2023 in Long Island City to connect to a larger base of volunteer and foster homes.
“We need foster homes that clear up space, and we can save more lives. If you’re not sure of a lifetime commitment, foster and see how it goes,” she says.
Brooks is a former schoolteacher. When Animal Care Centers of New York stopped taking pets due to overcrowding during the summer, a network of shelters stepped up.
It’s still at a crisis point.
“We’ve received more calls for help. We took as many as we could, but space and resources are limited,” she says.
Second Chance Rescue also has a location in Westchester County. Bad economic times also result in more pet surrenders.
More: Latest News from Around the Tri-State Second Chance Rescue estimates it has saved about 15,000 dogs and cats since it was founded in 2009 with the help of a community of donors and supporters.
They concentrate on large breed dogs and cats who need critical life-saving care because those two criteria are the common reasons for pet euthanasia in the U.S..
Nine out of ten animals that enter NYC Second Chance Rescue were once set to be euthanized at a municipal shelter, according to the group.
They ask pet owners to get animals spayed or neutered. The group can also help cover the cost of some pet health procedures or surgeries.
